config.title: useMediaQuery

intro.title: useMediaQuery
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular component that dynamically changes its text and style based on the screen width. You will learn how to use the `useMediaQuery` function from Angular CDK to detect and respond to changes in viewport size. The main technologies involved are Angular components, TypeScript, and reactive programming with observables. By the end, you will understand how to make your applications responsive and adaptive to different devices.
intro.usecase: The useMediaQuery pattern is essential for creating responsive applications that adapt to different screen sizes and device capabilities. In real-world Angular applications, developers use this to conditionally render dashboard components on large screens while showing simplified mobile views, adjust form layouts between desktop and tablet modes, and toggle navigation menus between full sidebar and hamburger menu styles. Product examples include e-commerce sites that rearrange product grids, analytics dashboards that show/hide detailed panels, and media players that switch control layouts based on available space. This pattern allows developers to build single codebases that deliver optimal user experiences across all devices.

objectives: Initialize a reactive media query subscription in an Angular component
Apply the BreakpointObserver service to detect viewport size changes
Configure conditional rendering based on media query results
Manipulate component state in response to breakpoint changes
Integrate media query logic with Angular's change detection system
Construct responsive UI components using the BreakpointObserver API
Bind component templates to media query state variables

steps.title: Import Component and CommonModule from @angular/core and @angular/common
steps.instruction: Import the Component decorator from '@angular/core' and the CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with the correct module paths. For example: import { Component } from '@angular/core';

steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have access to Angular's core decorator and common directives for the template.
successCriteria: Component is imported from '@angular/core' and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.

steps.hint: Use the import statement with curly braces to import both BreakpointObserver and Breakpoints from '@angular/cdk/layout'.

steps.title: Create the main AppComponent class with @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Define the AppComponent class with @Component decorator and selector 'app-root'.
steps.hint: Add the @Component decorator above the class definition and set the selector property to 'app-root'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class is defined with the @Component decorator and selector 'app-root'.
successCriteria: AppComponent class is exported with @Component decorator having selector: 'app-root'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the @Component decorator is properly configured with selector: 'app-root' and the class is exported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component definition is missing or incorrect. Check that you have the @Component decorator with selector 'app-root' and an exported class named AppComponent.

steps.title: Add template and styles to the @Component decorator
steps.instruction: Add the template and styles properties to the @Component decorator in your AppComponent class. Use a simple template with a heading and paragraph, and basic styles for demonstration.
steps.hint: The template property should contain HTML markup, and the styles property should contain CSS rules. Both are strings.
steps.expectedOutcome: The @Component decorator now includes template and styles properties with basic content and styling.
successCriteria: The @Component decorator has both template and styles properties defined as strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both template and styles properties are present and contain valid string values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component decorator is missing the required template and styles properties. Review the example and try again.

steps.title: Inject BreakpointObserver in the constructor
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, add a constructor that injects BreakpointObserver as a parameter.
steps.hint: Use the constructor keyword with a parameter of type BreakpointObserver. Angular's dependency injection will provide the service instance.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class will have a constructor that accepts BreakpointObserver as a parameter, enabling the use of media query observation.
successCriteria: Constructor is defined with a BreakpointObserver parameter injection.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a constructor with a BreakpointObserver parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor injection is missing or incorrect. Review Angular dependency injection syntax.

steps.title: Initialize isMobile state property as boolean
steps.instruction: Inside the AppComponent class, declare a property named 'isMobile' with type 'boolean' and initialize it to 'false'.
steps.hint: Add the property declaration directly in the class body, after the constructor if present.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class will have a boolean property 'isMobile' initialized to false, ready to store responsive breakpoint state.
successCriteria: The isMobile property is declared with type boolean and initial value false in the AppComponent class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure isMobile has the correct type (boolean) and is initialized to false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isMobile property isn't properly declared. Check that it has type boolean and initial value false.

steps.title: Create ngOnInit lifecycle method
steps.instruction: Add the ngOnInit lifecycle method to your AppComponent class to initialize the component.
steps.hint: In Angular, ngOnInit is a lifecycle hook that runs after the component is initialized. Add the method inside the class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The AppComponent class will have an ngOnInit method ready for initialization logic.
successCriteria: The ngOnInit method is defined inside the AppComponent class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the ngOnInit method inside the AppComponent class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method is missing or incorrectly placed. It should be a method inside the AppComponent class.

steps.title: Set up media query observation in ngOnInit
steps.instruction: Inside the ngOnInit method, call this.breakpointObserver.observe() with Breakpoints.Handset and subscribe to update the isMobile property.
steps.hint: Use the observe method on the injected breakpointObserver with the Handset breakpoint, then subscribe to the result to update isMobile.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ngOnInit method will now observe the Handset breakpoint and update isMobile when the viewport changes.
successCriteria: ngOnInit contains a call to breakpointObserver.observe with Breakpoints.Handset and a subscription that updates isMobile.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling observe with Breakpoints.Handset and subscribing to update isMobile.
steps.feedbackWrong: The ngOnInit method should observe the Handset breakpoint and update isMobile when the viewport changes.

steps.title: Add conditional rendering in template based on isMobile
steps.instruction: In the template property of the @Component decorator, add two paragraphs: one that shows 'Mobile view active' when isMobile is true using *ngIf, and another that shows 'Desktop view active' when isMobile is false using *ngIf with an else clause.
steps.hint: Use Angular's *ngIf directive with the else clause to conditionally render different content based on the boolean isMobile property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will conditionally display different messages for mobile and desktop views based on the isMobile state.
successCriteria: Template contains two paragraphs with *ngIf directives: one showing 'Mobile view active' when isMobile is true, and another showing 'Desktop view active' when isMobile is false using an else clause.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have both paragraphs with *ngIf directives and the else clause properly set up.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet have the required conditional rendering. Review how to use *ngIf with else in Angular templates.

steps.title: Add CSS styles for responsive layout demonstration
steps.instruction: Add CSS styles to the component's styles array to create a responsive layout that visually demonstrates the mobile detection.
steps.hint: Add CSS rules inside the styles array in the @Component decorator. Use the isMobile state to create visual differences between mobile and desktop views.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have CSS styles that create a responsive layout, making the mobile/desktop differences visually apparent when resizing the browser.
successCriteria: CSS styles are added to the styles array in the @Component decorator, including responsive rules that demonstrate the media query behavior.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some styles, but make sure they're in the styles array and include responsive rules that change based on screen size.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS styles weren't added correctly. Remember to add them inside the styles array in the @Component decorator.
